role_outputs.Research Analyst:
Overview

Costco runs membership warehouses and e-commerce sites on a low-price, high-volume model. The 10-K says the concept is that "offering low prices on a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products in a wide range of categories will produce high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover" [10-K.txt:L180]. The footprint is 939 warehouses, up from 914 a year earlier: "Costco operated 939, 914, and 890 warehouses worldwide at August 30, 2026, August 31, 2025, and September 1, 2024." [10-K.txt:L177]

Fiscal 2026 results (52 weeks ended August 30, 2026) are consistent with management's growth claim: "Net sales increased 10% to $297,247, driven by an increase in comparable sales and sales at new warehouses;" [10-K.txt:L709] and "Net income increased 14% to $9,226, $20.76 per diluted share, compared to $8,099, $18.21 per diluted share in 2025; and" [10-K.txt:L721].

Revenue concentration is the main structural exposure. "Our financial and operational performance is highly dependent on our U.S. and Canadian operations, which comprised 86% and 83% of net sales and operating income in 2026." [10-K.txt:L350] Within the U.S., "our California operations, which comprised 26% of U.S. net sales in 2026" [10-K.txt:L350]. Supplier concentration is not a stated issue: "We do not obtain a significant portion of merchandise from any one supplier." [10-K.txt:L211] Gasoline is a notable sales component: "Our gasoline business represented 11% of total net sales in 2026." [10-K.txt:L207]

Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

Criterion 1, Demand durability: SUPPORTED.
- Fiscal 2026 comparable sales were driven by both ticket and traffic: "Comparable sales were positively impacted by increases of 5% in average ticket and 3% in shopping frequency." [10-K.txt:L835]
- Paid members were 84,100 thousand at the end of 2026 versus 81,000 thousand at the end of 2025 [10-K.txt:L223] "84,100" [10-K.txt:L224] "81,000".
- Executive members were 42,300 thousand in 2026: "Executive members represented 42,300, 38,700, and 35,400 of total paid members in 2026, 2025, and 2024." [10-K.txt:L237]
- Renewal rates are high: "At the end of 2026, member renewal rates were 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide." [10-K.txt:L851]
- Membership fee revenue was $5,907 million in 2026: "Membership fee revenue increased 11% to $5,907, driven by new member sign-ups, membership fee increases, and upgrades to Executive membership;" [10-K.txt:L713]
- Digital demand is growing: "Digitally-enabled comparable sales increased 21% during 2026, both as reported and excluding the impact of changes in foreign currencies." [10-K.txt:L836]

Caveats on this criterion:
- Reported comparable sales are flattered by gasoline and currency. The release shows total company 52-week comparable sales of [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L36] "8.4%" versus adjusted (excluding gasoline prices and foreign exchange) of [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L37] "6.6%".
- Gasoline volume contributed: "The volume of gasoline sold increased 7%, positively impacting net sales by $1,913, or 71 basis points." [10-K.txt:L838]
- Digital sign-ups renew at a lower rate: "Our worldwide renewal rate is adversely impacted by membership growth in certain international markets and a higher penetration of memberships sold online, including through digital membership promotions, which renew at a slightly lower rate on average." [10-K.txt:L695]
- Prior-year renewal rates are not in the supplied extraction, so the renewal trend is not established by the supplied evidence.

Criterion 2, Competitive position: MIXED.
- Supporting: operating income rose to $11,685 million in fiscal 2026 [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L102] "11,685" from $10,383 million in fiscal 2025 [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L103] "10,383". SG&A leverage was positive on a reported basis: "SG&A expenses as a percentage of net sales decreased 10 basis points; it increased one basis point excluding the impact of gasoline price inflation;" [10-K.txt:L717]
- Core merchandise margin improved on its own sales base: "The gross margin in core merchandise categories when expressed as a percentage of their own sales increased 15 basis points." [10-K.txt:L885]
- Employee retention supports the operating model: "In 2026, in the U.S. and Canada that rate was approximately 94% for employees who have been with us for at least one year." [10-K.txt:L266]
- Weakening: consolidated gross margin slipped: "Gross margin percentage decreased three basis points." [10-K.txt:L884] SG&A pressure appears abroad: "SG&A expenses as a percentage of net sales increased in our Canadian and Other International segments and were flat in our U.S. segment compared to 2025." [10-K.txt:L905]
- Mix is working against core margin: "The majority of the increase in warehouse ancillary and other businesses and the decrease in core merchandise categories was due to the change in sales mix" [10-K.txt:L884].
- Management asserts competitive standing but gives no share data. Named rivals include: "Walmart, Target, Kroger, and Amazon are among our significant general merchandise retail competitors in the U.S." [10-K.txt:L275] The filing also concedes: "Some competitors have greater technology capabilities, including the faster adoption of AI technologies, and greater market penetration than we do." [10-K.txt:L395]
- Kirkland Signature sales penetration is a claimed advantage: "We expect to continue to increase the sales penetration of our private-label items." [10-K.txt:L277] A private-label sales figure is not established by the supplied evidence.

Criterion 3, Growth execution: SUPPORTED, with rising cost and execution risk.
- Openings: "We opened 28 new warehouses, including three relocations, for a total of 25 net new warehouses: 18 in the U.S., five in our Canadian segment, and two in our Other International segment, compared to 27 new warehouses, including three relocations, in 2025;" [10-K.txt:L707]
- Investment is stepping up: fiscal 2026 additions to property and equipment were [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L310] "(6,435)", and the plan is [10-K.txt:L1009] "our current intention to spend approximately $7,500 du" (the extraction breaks the sentence; fiscal 2027 follows at L1010-L1012). Fiscal 2027 openings: "plan to open up to 33 new warehouses, including five relocations, in 2027" [10-K.txt:L1018].
- Funding capacity: "Net cash provided by operating activities totaled $15,817 in 2026, compared to $13,335 in 2025." [10-K.txt:L1000] "These expenditures are expected to be financed with cash from operations, cash and cash equivalents, and short-term investments." [10-K.txt:L1013]
- Data discrepancy: the earnings release shows operating cash flow of [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L306] "15,825" against the 10-K's $15,817 million. The release labels its statements "Subject to Reclassification" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L277], so I rely on the 10-K figure.
- International runway is disclosed: "we operated 292 warehouses outside of the U.S. (31% of all warehouse locations), and we plan to continue expanding our international operations" [10-K.txt:L425]. International contributes disproportionately to profit: "our international operations, including Canada, generated 27% and 35% of our net sales and operating income" [10-K.txt:L407].
- Cost of expansion is acknowledged: "Negative aspects of such growth include lower initial operating profitability relative to existing warehouses and cannibalization of sales at existing warehouses when openings occur in existing markets." [10-K.txt:L694] Also: "As our warehouse base grows and available and desirable sites become more difficult to secure, square footage growth becomes a comparatively less substantial component of growth." [10-K.txt:L694]
- Non-warehouse investments carry less certainty: "The effectiveness of these investments can be less predictable than opening new locations and might not provide the anticipated benefits or desired rates of return." [10-K.txt:L357]

Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

Catalysts and developments:
- Warehouse openings and capital spending continue to rise, per the fiscal 2027 plan cited above [10-K.txt:L1018].
- Tariff refunds are a non-recurring tailwind. "This year's fourth quarter was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values." [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L44] Fiscal 2026 gross margin includes it: "IEEPA tariff refunds, net of investment in price reductions for members, positively impacted gross margin by three basis points." [10-K.txt:L884] Further refunds are expected, with most to be reinvested in member value: "Subsequent to 2026, we received $155 in additional refunds and we intend to continue to invest the majority of the refunds in increased value for the member." [10-K.txt:L726]
- Labor cost is rising by design: "bringing our average rate at the end of 2026 for hourly employees in the U.S. to approximately $33.00" [10-K.txt:L270].
- Expectations are high: "We believe that the price of our stock currently reflects high market expectations for our future operating results." [10-K.txt:L417]

Analyst recommendations (judgments, not company statements):
1. Test growth quality by separating gasoline, currency and tariff-refund effects from underlying comparable sales and gross margin. The adjusted comparable figure was [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L37] "6.6%", versus reported [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L36] "8.4%".
2. Track international SG&A as the expansion cost indicator. Canadian and Other International SG&A ratios rose in fiscal 2026 [10-K.txt:L905], while openings are planned to accelerate [10-K.txt:L1018].
3. Watch the effect of digital membership acquisition on renewal rates, given the disclosed lower renewal rate for online sign-ups [10-K.txt:L695].

What would change my view: my strongest conclusion is that demand durability is supported. A next-filing worldwide member renewal rate below the current 89.8% [10-K.txt:L851] "At the end of 2026, member renewal rates were 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide.", especially alongside continued paid-member growth, would challenge it. The filing says digitally sourced memberships renew at a slightly lower rate [10-K.txt:L695], so a decline would indicate that growth is increasingly coming from lower-retention cohorts.

Insight: Membership fee revenue growth of 11% to $5,907 million in fiscal 2026 leaned less on the September 2024 fee increase than in fiscal 2025, since the fee increase's share of membership income growth fell from approximately 40% to approximately 30%, meaning more of the growth now depends on member sign-ups and Executive upgrades. [10-K.txt:L854] "The fee income increase accounted for approximately 30% and 40% of membership income growth during 2026 and 2025."
role_outputs.Financial Analyst:
COST (FY ended 2026-08-30): Valuation Insights

Scope note: I did not calculate anything. Every ratio below is a supplied calculation, labelled "computed, rechecked given calculations", with its arithmetic and input citations reproduced. Calculations I could not take from the supplied data are listed in calculator_requests.

1. CASH GENERATION: SUPPORTED
- Operating cash flow was 15,817,000,000 [XBRL tag NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093]. The prior year was 13,335,000,000 [same tag, period end 2025-08-31, filing 0000909832-25-000101].
- Capital spending was 6,435,000,000 [XBRL tag PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093]. The prior year was 5,498,000,000 [same tag, period end 2025-08-31, filing 0000909832-25-000101].
- Free cash flow (computed, rechecked given calculations): 15,817,000,000 - 6,435,000,000 = 9,382,000,000 USD. Inputs: the two FY2026 tags cited above.
- Prior-year free cash flow, capex as a share of operating cash flow, and growth rates were not supplied. I have requested them.
- Revenue of 303,154,000,000 versus 275,235,000,000 [XBRL tag RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax, period ends 2026-08-30 and 2025-08-31, filings 0000909832-26-000093 and 0000909832-25-000101] is supported by operating cash flow that exceeds capex.
- Supplied revenue growth (computed, rechecked given calculations): (303154000000 - 275235000000) / 275235000000 = 10.143695387577887%.
- Cash financing activity: net cash used in financing activities was $3,355 in 2026 versus $3,775 in 2025 [10-K.txt:L1020]. Dollar amounts in 10-K lines are as shown in the filing text.

2. PROFITABILITY: SUPPORTED, WITH THIN-MARGIN CONTEXT
- Operating margin (computed, rechecked given calculations): 11685000000 / 303154000000 = 3.8544766026507977%. Definition: operating income divided by total revenue. Inputs: [XBRL tag OperatingIncomeLoss, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093] and [XBRL tag RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093].
- Return on average equity (computed, rechecked given calculations): 9226000000 / ((35803000000 + 29164000000) / 2) = 28.402111841396398%. Definition: reported net income fact divided by the simple average of current and prior year-end stockholders' equity. Inputs:
  - [XBRL tag NetIncomeLoss, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093]
  - [XBRL tag StockholdersEquity, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093]
  - [XBRL tag StockholdersEquity, period end 2025-08-31, filing 0000909832-25-000101]
- Noncontrolling interest income is not available in the supplied XBRL data (tag null). The supplied 10-K passages do not address it, so it is not established by the supplied evidence. The numerator is therefore the NetIncomeLoss fact, which the supplied data also uses as net income attributable to parent.
- Peer operating margins as supplied (computed, rechecked given calculations by the supplied peer data):
  - WMT 4.182073382943311% (period end 2026-01-31)
  - TGT 4.8835655659477% (period end 2026-01-31)
  - BJ 3.8057210808791457% (period end 2026-01-31)
  - Comparability limit: the peers' periods end 2026-01-31, about seven months before COST's 2026-08-30. This is a loose comparison only.
- Peer return on equity was not supplied.

3. FUNDING RISK: SUPPORTED, WITH A DEFINITION LIMIT
- Debt to equity (computed, rechecked given calculations): (3914000000 + 2248000000) / 35803000000 = 0.17210848252939698 ratio.
- Debt components included, with the current portion counted once:
  - [XBRL tag LongTermDebtNoncurrent, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093] = 3,914,000,000
  - [XBRL tag LongTermDebtCurrent, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093] = 2,248,000,000
  - Denominator: [XBRL tag StockholdersEquity, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093] = 35,803,000,000
- Excluded by the supplied definition: repos, secured financings, and lease liabilities not captured by the selected debt tags.
- Debt structure moved toward near-term maturities. LongTermDebtNoncurrent was 5,713,000,000 at 2025-08-31 and LongTermDebtCurrent was 75,000,000 at 2025-08-31 [filing 0000909832-25-000101]. At 2026-08-30 they were 3,914,000,000 and 2,248,000,000. The cash balance was not supplied, so coverage of the current portion is not established by the supplied evidence.
- ShortTermBorrowings is not available in the supplied XBRL data. The supplied filing passages say:
  - "There were no short-term borrowings outstanding under the bank credit facilities at the end of 2026." [10-K.txt:L1030]. This is limited to the bank credit facilities, so I do not treat it as zero for all short-term debt.
  - "There were no short-term borrowings outstanding at the end of 2026, and short-term borrowings were immaterial at the end of 2025." [10-K.txt:L2278, Note 4, Short-Term Borrowings]. This appears in the note on the bank credit facilities. The supplied D/E does not include any short-term borrowing amount.
- Borrowing capacity under bank credit facilities was $2,118 at August 30, 2026 [10-K.txt:L1030]. The U.S. revolver was extended to August 2027 [10-K.txt:L1030], so the facilities themselves mature within a year.
- Peer debt to equity was not supplied. Peer debt components differ: WMT reports ShortTermBorrowings of 6,596,000,000 [XBRL tag ShortTermBorrowings, period end 2026-01-31, filing 0000104169-26-000055], while TGT and BJ have no ShortTermBorrowings value supplied. I will not compare funding ratios until the same definition is computed for all.

4. VALUATION: UNSUPPORTED AS A RELATIVE-VALUE CLAIM; ABSOLUTE P/E SUPPLIED
- P/E (computed, rechecked given calculations): 992.13 / 20.76 = 47.79046242774566 ratio.
- Price source: user-supplied --price at run time 2026-11-05T09:09:24-05:00. The market quote timestamp was not provided.
- EPS input: [XBRL tag EarningsPerShareDiluted, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093] = 20.76. The prior year was 18.21 [same tag, period end 2025-08-31, filing 0000909832-25-000101].
- Peer P/E is not available. No peer prices were supplied, though peer diluted EPS was: WMT 2.73, TGT 8.13, BJ 4.38, all for period end 2026-01-31. I cannot state that COST's multiple is high or low versus peers without peer prices on a comparable date. Peer P/E is requested below. Peer fiscal periods also differ from COST's.
- EPS context: Q4 net income was $2.998 billion, or $6.75 per diluted share, versus $2.610 billion, or $5.87, a year earlier. Q4 "was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values." [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L44]
- Supplied share of full-year EPS (computed, rechecked given calculations): 0.15 / 20.76 * 100 = 0.722543352601156%. Inputs: the earnings release L44 quote above and [XBRL tag EarningsPerShareDiluted, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093].

5. LATEST QUARTER
- Total revenue was 95,723 versus 86,156 [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L83-L85; quote: "Total revenue\n95,723\n86,156"].
- Quarter revenue growth (computed, rechecked given calculations): (95723.0 - 86156.0) / 86156.0 * 100 = 11.104275964529458%.
- GAAP diluted EPS was $6.75 [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L137-L137; quote: "6.75"]. No adjusted EPS flags were supplied.

6. WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY VIEW
- Measure: next reported free cash flow. The current cited value is 9,382,000,000 [computed from XBRL tags NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities and PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093].
- A decline below this level, for example if capex grows faster than operating cash flow, would weaken my view. At 47.79 times EPS, the valuation depends on cash-funded growth continuing.

Insight: Costco's growth in FY2026 was funded internally, and the non-recurring tariff-refund benefit explains very little of the EPS behind the P/E: operating cash flow covered capex with 9,382,000,000 of free cash flow left, while the $0.15 refund benefit was only 0.722543352601156% of FY EPS. [Computed, rechecked given calculations: free cash flow = 15817000000 - 6435000000 = 9382000000 USD, from XBRL tag NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities and XBRL tag PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093; refund share = 0.15 / 20.76 * 100 = 0.722543352601156%, from earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L44 quote "non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds" and XBRL tag EarningsPerShareDiluted, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093]
role_outputs.Investment Advisor:
Recommendation: Hold.

Thesis: The business and financial evidence agree that Costco is a high-quality compounder, but the supplied valuation does not show enough support to add. The Research Analyst finds demand durability supported: net income rose 14% to $9,226, or $20.76 per diluted share [10-K.txt:L721]; paid members reached 84,100 thousand [10-K.txt:L223]; and worldwide renewal was 89.8% [10-K.txt:L851]. The Financial Analyst finds cash generation supported: operating cash flow was 15,817,000,000 [XBRL tag NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093], and free cash flow was 9,382,000,000 (computed, rechecked given calculations: 15,817,000,000 - 6,435,000,000, from NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities and PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment). Growth was funded internally. Operating margin was 3.8544766026507977% (computed, rechecked given calculations; OperatingIncomeLoss 11,685,000,000 over RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax 303,154,000,000, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093).

Criteria:
1. Thesis support: SUPPORTED. The business and financial evidence align. Revenue growth was 10.143695387577887% (computed, rechecked given calculations; same revenue tag, period ends 2026-08-30 and 2025-08-31). Net sales rose 10% to $297,247 [10-K.txt:L709]. Quality caveat: reported total-company comparable sales were 8.4% [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L36] against 6.6% adjusted for gasoline prices and foreign exchange [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L37]. Operating cash flow also differs between the 10-K ($15,817 million) and the earnings release (15,825, labelled "Subject to Reclassification" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L277]). I use the 10-K and XBRL figure, as the Research Analyst did.
2. Downside exposure: MIXED. Leverage is low: debt to equity was 0.17210848252939698 ratio (computed, rechecked given calculations; LongTermDebtNoncurrent 3,914,000,000 + LongTermDebtCurrent 2,248,000,000 over StockholdersEquity 35,803,000,000, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093). However, LongTermDebtCurrent was 75,000,000 at 2025-08-31 [filing 0000909832-25-000101], so debt moved toward near-term maturity. The cash balance was not supplied, so coverage of the current portion is not established by the supplied evidence. Facility-specific limit: "There were no short-term borrowings outstanding under the bank credit facilities at the end of 2026" [10-K.txt:L1030]. This applies only to those facilities, not to all short-term debt. ShortTermBorrowings is missing from the structured data, and the supplied D/E includes no short-term borrowing amount. Borrowing capacity under the facilities was $2,118 at August 30, 2026, and the U.S. revolver was extended to August 2027 [10-K.txt:L1030]. Operating risks: capex was 6,435,000,000 [XBRL tag PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093] against a stated intention to spend approximately $7,500 [10-K.txt:L1009]. U.S. and Canadian operations were 86% of net sales and 83% of operating income [10-K.txt:L350]. Consolidated gross margin fell three basis points [10-K.txt:L884]. Canadian and Other International SG&A ratios rose [10-K.txt:L905]. None of this undermines the thesis today, but expansion costs are rising.
3. Valuation support: UNSUPPORTED as a relative-value claim for adding. The only supplied multiple is an absolute P/E of 47.79046242774566 ratio (computed, rechecked given calculations: 992.13 / 20.76; EPS from XBRL tag EarningsPerShareDiluted, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093). The price is user-supplied at run time 2026-11-05T09:09:24-05:00, and the market quote timestamp was not provided. Peer prices and P/Es were not supplied, so I cannot say the multiple is high or low versus peers. Peer fiscal periods also end 2026-01-31, which makes comparison loose. The filing itself says: "We believe that the price of our stock currently reflects high market expectations for our future operating results." [10-K.txt:L417]. The non-recurring tariff benefit is small: $0.15 per diluted share [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L44], or 0.722543352601156% of FY EPS (computed, rechecked given calculations: 0.15 / 20.76 * 100).

Deciding number: P/E of 47.79046242774566 ratio (computed, rechecked given calculations: 992.13 / 20.76; EPS from XBRL tag EarningsPerShareDiluted, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093). It carries the most weight because the business and cash evidence is already strong and largely agreed between the analysts. What remains unresolved is whether the price pays for it, and the supplied evidence cannot show that the multiple is cheap.

Main risk: The multiple leaves little room for slippage. Rising capex and near-term debt maturities, together with the lower-renewing digital member cohorts the filing describes [10-K.txt:L695], could reduce cash-funded growth. The Financial Analyst states that at this multiple the valuation depends on cash-funded growth continuing.

What would change the rating: Next-filing free cash flow below the current 9,382,000,000 (computed from NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities and PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093), for example if capex grows faster than operating cash flow, would move my view toward Sell. Free cash flow at or above that level would keep the Hold, and peer P/E evidence on a comparable date would be needed before upgrading to Buy.

Insight: At 47.79046242774566 times FY2026 diluted EPS of 20.76, Costco's valuation depends on cash-funded growth continuing, and FY2026 free cash flow of 9,382,000,000 shows that growth was internally funded this year. [Computed, rechecked given calculations: P/E = 992.13 / 20.76, EPS from XBRL tag EarningsPerShareDiluted, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093; free cash flow = 15,817,000,000 - 6,435,000,000, from XBRL tag NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities and XBRL tag PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, period end 2026-08-30, filing 0000909832-26-000093]
